sentences.text:
This is an application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
2.

The petitioner is an accused in connection with Cyber Crime P.S. Case No.6 of 2024 corresponding to C.T. Case No.232 of 2024 for the offences under Sections 420/467/120-B/34 of I.P.C. read with Section 66(D) of the I.T. Act pending in the Court of the learned S.D.J.M.,

entities.text: Cyber Crime P.S. Case No.6 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The petitioner had approached the learned Court below praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 03.10.2024 has rejected the bail application of the petitioner.

Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
praying for enlargement on bail.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner submits that except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
4.

The prosecution case in short is that, the informant lodged a written report before the CID, CB Cyber P.S. alleging therein that the accused-petitioner had approached him to invest money in his crypto currency trading for getting more profit.
It is alleged by the informant that he gave Rs.71,85,000/- to the petitioner and initially the petitioner paid profit for some months and thereafter stopped payment.

When the informant asked the money, the petitioner issued cheques,
which were bounced on presentation for encashment.

Hence, the F.I.R.
5.
The dispute is arising out of monetary transaction in a business being carried out by the petitioner and the informant.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has already paid Muntaj Ali vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party(S) on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18444883/
1 about Rs.12 lakhs to the informant which is being disputed by the informant.
6.

entities.text: Muntaj Ali vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party(S)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner on instruction from his client voluntarily makes a statement before this Court that his client would deposit Rs.10, 00,000/- (Rupees ten lakhs) and would try to resolve the dispute by paying the rest of the amount to the informant and put a quitous to the entire dispute.
However, he may be enlarged on bail so that he can arrange the money to make good the same.

The petitioner is in custody since 06.02.2024.
7.

Since the dispute hinges upon the monetary transaction between the petitioner and the informant and the petitioner has voluntarily made a statement that he would deposit Rs.10, 00,000/-, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail subject to the petitioner depositing Rs.10, 00,000/-as pre-condition as per his own offer.

Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper, subject to the following additional conditions:-
(i) The petitioner shall appear before the trial Court on each date on which the case is posted for trial.
(ii) He shall not tamper with the evidence in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) He shall not involve in any similar type of offence.
(iv) He shall be release subject to verification antecedents.

In the event, the petitioner is found to be wanted of violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.

(S.S. Mishra) Judge Swarna Location: High Court of Orissa Muntaj Ali vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party(S) on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18444883/
